answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit work, with rewards weighted by stake and penalties triggered by independently verified fraud. Creating a hundred aliases then does not multiply influence for free: the attacker must divide or multiply capital, while one proven lie can burn the stake behind every exposed identity. The orchard of agents may include an ember or quartz as a name, but names alone earn no weight; capital at risk makes Sybil identities costly.
